submitter: bugfix_277_required_fields_repair lane — content_data recovery by template inversion, gated on a byte-identical round-trip. Owner instruction 2026-08-22: 'backfill the 27, scoped to these 27'. Migration 540 is APPLIED (3 rows); the tool is committed with it.
rationale:
27 page_components carry a parked `required_fields_missing` finding routed `no_content_data`: they hold rendered_html and NO content_data, serve correctly, and cannot be rebuilt from their own stored data. The owner asked for a backfill scoped to those 27.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT DICTATES THE DESIGN. datahelpers.ContentDataCanFillTemplate (template_reproducibility.go:71-81) returns true when content_data holds ANY ONE of the template's top-level fields. So writing a single recovered field flips a component from 'cannot regenerate' to 'can regenerate', and the next regeneration renders the template with that one field and blanks every other under missingkey=zero — the 004/007 blanking family, and the exact reason these rows were parked rather than repaired (auto-regeneration would REPLACE served HTML). A PARTIAL backfill is therefore not a smaller version of the right fix; it is a destructive one. The only safe output is a content_data that re-renders to the stored rendered_html byte for byte, because that property says precisely what needs to be true: what a regeneration would produce is what is being served today.

WHAT THE TOOL DOES. It inverts the component template against its own rendered_html — a backtracking matcher over text/template/parse, not a compiled regex, because RE2 has no backreferences and returns only the last match of a repeated group, so {{range}} bodies cannot be recovered in one pass, and {{if}}/{{else}} needs 'try this branch, and if the REST fails, try the other'. It then re-executes the template with the recovered data through the same execution path the estate renders components with (text/template, missingkey=zero, actions.executeGoTemplate's FuncMap, '<no value>' stripped as RenderTemplate does) and refuses anything that is not byte-identical. Templates that read RenderContext keys (domain, colors, nav, year…) are refused outright: those values do not come from content_data, so a match would prove nothing about a real render.

THE RESULT IS THE FINDING, not a shortfall. Over all 27: 3 recovered and proven; 7 blocked by template drift confined to <style>; 8 blocked by drift in MARKUP; 9 that must NOT be backfilled at all because the stored HTML is not that component's output — a whole interactive tool page (9.5–21.8KB) held in a slot pointing at `hero`, where a backfill would let a regeneration swap a working tool for a 2KB hero band. The 15 drifted rows were rendered by template versions that no longer exist: component_versions holds 367 rows across 202 components and ZERO for any of the nine components involved, so the original cannot be recovered and the proof cannot be met. They stay parked with the facts, which is today's behaviour.

plan.summary: Add cmd/content-data-recover (template inversion + a byte-identical round-trip gate), and apply migration 540 writing the three recoveries it can prove. Refuse the other 24, with the reason measured per row.

edits.rationale: The gate and the refusals. recoverRow parses the template, refuses any that reads a RenderContext key, runs the matcher, and then re-executes with the recovered data and demands the exact stored bytes. funcMap mirrors actions.executeGoTemplate's FuncMap so the verification renders the way production renders; if that map gains a function, a template using it fails to PARSE here and is reported unsupported — a safe direction, but a silent loss of coverage, stated in the file. Input is JSON on stdin (the estate's kubectl-exec-psql export convention, as in cmd/config-key-audit) so the tool holds no credentials; -sql emits guarded UPDATEs on stdout.

The inverter, in continuation-passing style so an {{if}} can backtrack when the REST of the template fails. Two refusals live here rather than in the gate because the gate CANNOT catch them: an unattributable pipeline ({{or .a .b}} renders identically whichever field held the value, so a wrong attribution would round-trip) and a nested field (.a.b). candidateEnds anchors each value on the following literal, which is what stops nested actions exploding combinatorially; maxSteps is the backstop. Everything this file produces is a guess until the round-trip proves it — that division is deliberate and stated at the top.

Three recovery tests and six refusal controls, so the suite cannot be satisfied by a function that always accepts OR always refuses. THE POINT WORTH REVIEWING: my first mutation of the round-trip gate PASSED — disabling it left the suite green, because every control was caught earlier by the matcher (a guard in series). The named test exists to isolate the gate: the matcher binds subheadline="" and takes the {{if}} branch, but re-rendering with "" makes the {{if}} false and the block vanishes, so only the gate can reject it. With the gate disabled that test, and only that test, fails.

Writes the three proven recoveries and nothing else. Guards are WHERE-clause conditions rather than pre-checks, so a row that moved since the export updates 0 rows instead of being written wrongly: content_data IS NULL (refuses to overwrite anything written since) and md5(rendered_html) = the digest the proof was taken against (the proof is about THOSE bytes; a re-rendered component must be re-proven). Pre-image goes to page_components_bak_20260822_277_recover per the estate's page_components_bak_* convention, so the ROLLBACK is a restore rather than a reconstruction. Verify block RAISEs on three things: 3 rows carry content_data, ZERO rendered_html digests changed (this migration writes data, never markup), and the backup holds 3 NULL pre-images. Exercised: COMMIT→ROLLBACK dry run (3 UPDATEs, verify NOTICE), and an induced failure (plant content_data on one row first → aborts rather than writing a partial set).

   AND content_data IS NULL

plan.risks: Making a component fillable is a real change in kind: before, no regenerate route could reach it; after, they can. That is licensed here only by the byte-identical round-trip, which says a regeneration reproduces what is served today — and it is why the 24 unproven rows were left alone rather than written with a looser gate. The three writes are data-only and the verify asserts zero rendered_html digests changed, so no visitor-visible change occurs at write time. The tool's funcMap must track executeGoTemplate's: if that map gains a function, templates using it fail to parse here and are silently reported unsupported (safe direction, stated in the file, but it is a coverage cliff rather than an error). The 9 tool-page-in-a-hero-slot rows are a separate defect and are being filed separately; nothing here touches them, and a future general 'fill any empty content_data' mechanism MUST exclude them or a regeneration would swap a working 16KB tool for a 2KB hero band.
